The diagram shows that the parabola is horizontal, has its vertex at $(-3,-1),$ and passes through the point $(-5,1).$

The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=p{t}^{2},\,y-k=2pt,
$$

where $p$ is constant.

In our case, $(h,k)=(-3,-1),$ and so we have

$$
x+3=p{t}^{2},\,y+1=2pt.
$$

Since the parabola passes through $(-5,1),$ we can substitute $x=-5$ and $y=1$ into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-2=p{t}^{2} \\ 2=2pt.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the second equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =2pt \\ 1 & =pt \\ t & =\frac{1}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the first equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2 & =p{(\frac{1}{p})}^{2} \\ -2 & =p\cdot \frac{1}{{p}^{2}} \\ -2 & =\frac{1}{p} \\ p & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x+3=(-\frac{1}{2}){t}^{2},\,y+1=2(-\frac{1}{2})t,
$$

which simplify to

$$
x+3=-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2},\,y+1=-t.
$$
